plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: In late spring, whole streets in the Southern Hemisphere fill with trees covered in lavender-blue trumpet flowers. The blossoms drift down and carpet the pavement in purple. From a distance the canopies look like clouds of violet mist.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in October and early November, with flowers lasting up to two months
plants.location: Pretoria (Tshwane), South Africa, and other Southern Hemisphere cities
plants.funFact: Jacarandas are native to South America, but Pretoria has so many of them that it is nicknamed the Jacaranda City.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub flowers in autumn, when most other camellias are still in bud. Its delicate, often lightly fragrant blooms open flat, with a golden boss of stamens at the center. Petals fall in soft drifts beneath the plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, usually starting in October or November
plants.location: Gardens in Japan, its native home, and in the warm-temperate southern United States
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed for oil in parts of Asia.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Bare, leafless stems rise from the garden soil and carry rounded clusters of bright pink flowers with wavy, sparkling petals. They bring exotic color just as the autumn border is fading. Their glitter-like sheen catches the low autumn light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, commonly October and into November
plants.location: Gardens in the United Kingdom and temperate Europe; native to South Africa's mountains
plants.funFact: Bowden lilies bloom best when their bulbs are crowded and baked by summer sun, so gardeners often plant them at the foot of a sunny wall.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Cosmos has airy, feathery foliage and daisy-like flowers that nod on slender stems in the autumn breeze. Its saucer-shaped blooms in pink, white and magenta attract bees and butterflies late in the season. In its homeland it colors roadsides and meadows.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through fall, continuing into autumn
plants.location: Native to Mexico; widely grown in gardens and meadows across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Its genus name comes from the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony, a nod to its neatly arranged petals.
